key_insight: At Re = 1000, adding a hemispherical leading-edge curvature changes separation and vortex shedding, producing thicker vortical regions and earlier shedding onset than a simple flat plate.
engineering_relevance: Leading-edge geometry can be tuned to trade off glide ratio and unsteady loading for low-Re small UAV or aquatic vehicle design.
method: Angle of attack sweep from 0° to 25°
Comparison of simple flat plate vs. plate with hemispherical leading-edge curvature at Re = 1000
evidence_signal: The abstract reports changes in shedding onset, shedding frequencies, force-coefficient spectra, and glide ratio across angles of attack, with the curved plate showing onset at 5° and multiple force frequencies at higher angles.
watch_item: Results are based on 2D simulations at a single Reynolds number, so 3D effects and broader operating conditions may limit direct transfer to real hardware.
paper_title: Effect of leading edge geometry on aerodynamic performance of a flat plate
